import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 64
DEPTH = 2
HEAD = 32


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.footprints = [(int(fp[0]), int(fp[1])) for fp in spec.footprints]
        layers, c_in = [], spec.in_channels
        for _ in range(DEPTH):
            layers += [nn.Conv2d(c_in, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU()]
            c_in = WIDTH
        self.body = nn.Sequential(*layers)
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, HEAD, 1)
        self.heads = nn.ModuleList([
            nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(3 * HEAD, HEAD, 1), nn.ReLU(), nn.Conv2d(HEAD, 1, 1))
            for _ in self.footprints
        ])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.body(obs)
        p = self.proj(f)
        outs = []
        for (dy, dx), head in zip(self.footprints, self.heads):
            pp = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            mx = F.max_pool2d(pp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            av = F.avg_pool2d(pp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            outs.append(head(torch.cat([p, mx, av], dim=1)))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import math
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

WIDTH = 64
DEPTH = 2


def init_layer(m, gain):
    nn.init.orthogonal_(m.weight, gain)
    nn.init.zeros_(m.bias)
    return m


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        g2 = math.sqrt(2.0)
        layers, c_in = [], spec.in_channels
        for _ in range(DEPTH):
            layers += [init_layer(nn.Conv2d(c_in, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), g2), nn.ReLU()]
            c_in = WIDTH
        self.body = nn.Sequential(*layers)
        self.place_head = init_layer(nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, spec.n_types, 1), 0.01)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(init_layer(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), g2), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = init_layer(nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1), 0.01)
        self.value_head = init_layer(nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1), 1.0)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.body(obs)
        place = self.place_head(f).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 32
BLOCKS = 2
HEAD = 16
LH = 24


class Block(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c):
        super().__init__()
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(c, c, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(c, c, 3, padding=1)

    def forward(self, x):
        return x + self.c2(F.relu(self.c1(F.relu(x))))


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.Z = int(spec.Z)
        self.footprints = [(int(fp[0]), int(fp[1])) for fp in spec.footprints]
        self.layer_in = nn.Conv2d(13, LH, 1)
        self.glob_in = nn.Conv2d(3, LH, 1)
        self.layer_mid = nn.Conv2d(LH, LH, 1)
        self.stem = nn.Conv2d(2 * LH, WIDTH, 1)
        self.register_buffer("zpos", torch.arange(self.Z).float() / max(self.Z - 1, 1))
        self.blocks = nn.Sequential(*[Block(WIDTH) for _ in range(BLOCKS)])
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, HEAD, 1)
        self.heads = nn.ModuleList([
            nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(3 * HEAD, HEAD, 1), nn.ReLU(), nn.Conv2d(HEAD, 1, 1))
            for _ in self.footprints
        ])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B, _, Y, X = obs.shape
        Z = self.Z
        v = obs[:, :4 * Z].reshape(B, 4, Z, Y, X)
        pz = F.pad(v, (0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1))
        below = pz[:, :, :Z]
        above = pz[:, :, 2:]
        zc = self.zpos.to(obs.dtype).view(1, 1, Z, 1, 1).expand(B, 1, Z, Y, X)
        x = torch.cat([v, below, above, zc], dim=1)
        x = x.permute(0, 2, 1, 3, 4).reshape(B * Z, 13, Y, X)
        gl = self.glob_in(obs[:, 4 * Z:4 * Z + 3]).unsqueeze(1)
        h = self.layer_in(x).reshape(B, Z, LH, Y, X) + gl
        h = F.relu(h).reshape(B * Z, LH, Y, X)
        h = F.relu(self.layer_mid(h)).reshape(B, Z, LH, Y, X)
        s = torch.cat([h.amax(1), h.mean(1)], dim=1)
        f = F.relu(self.blocks(self.stem(s)))
        p = self.proj(f)
        outs = []
        for (dy, dx), head in zip(self.footprints, self.heads):
            pp = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            mx = F.max_pool2d(pp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            av = F.avg_pool2d(pp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            outs.append(head(torch.cat([p, mx, av], dim=1)))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 32
BLOCKS = 2
HEAD = 16
LH = 24
LQ = 6


class Block(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c):
        super().__init__()
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(c, c, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(c, c, 3, padding=1)

    def forward(self, x):
        return x + self.c2(F.relu(self.c1(F.relu(x))))


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.Z = int(spec.Z)
        self.footprints = [(int(fp[0]), int(fp[1])) for fp in spec.footprints]
        self.layer_in = nn.Conv2d(13, LH, 1)
        self.glob_in = nn.Conv2d(3, LH, 1)
        self.layer_mid = nn.Conv2d(LH, LH, 1)
        self.stem = nn.Conv2d(2 * LH, WIDTH, 1)
        self.register_buffer("zpos", torch.arange(self.Z).float() / max(self.Z - 1, 1))
        self.blocks = nn.Sequential(*[Block(WIDTH) for _ in range(BLOCKS)])
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, HEAD, 1)
        self.heads = nn.ModuleList([
            nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(3 * HEAD, HEAD, 1), nn.ReLU(), nn.Conv2d(HEAD, 1, 1))
            for _ in self.footprints
        ])
        self.lproj = nn.Conv2d(LH, LQ, 1)
        self.lheads = nn.ModuleList([
            nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(3 * LQ, LQ, 1), nn.ReLU(), nn.Conv2d(LQ, 1, 1))
            for _ in self.footprints
        ])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B, _, Y, X = obs.shape
        Z = self.Z
        v = obs[:, :4 * Z].reshape(B, 4, Z, Y, X)
        pz = F.pad(v, (0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1))
        below = pz[:, :, :Z]
        above = pz[:, :, 2:]
        zc = self.zpos.to(obs.dtype).view(1, 1, Z, 1, 1).expand(B, 1, Z, Y, X)
        x = torch.cat([v, below, above, zc], dim=1)
        x = x.permute(0, 2, 1, 3, 4).reshape(B * Z, 13, Y, X)
        gl = self.glob_in(obs[:, 4 * Z:4 * Z + 3]).unsqueeze(1)
        h = self.layer_in(x).reshape(B, Z, LH, Y, X) + gl
        h = F.relu(h).reshape(B * Z, LH, Y, X)
        h = F.relu(self.layer_mid(h))
        q = self.lproj(h)
        h5 = h.reshape(B, Z, LH, Y, X)
        s = torch.cat([h5.amax(1), h5.mean(1)], dim=1)
        f = F.relu(self.blocks(self.stem(s)))
        p = self.proj(f)
        outs = []
        for (dy, dx), head, lhead in zip(self.footprints, self.heads, self.lheads):
            pp = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            mx = F.max_pool2d(pp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            av = F.avg_pool2d(pp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            main = head(torch.cat([p, mx, av], dim=1))
            qq = F.pad(q, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            lm = F.max_pool2d(qq, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            la = F.avg_pool2d(qq, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            ls = lhead(torch.cat([q, lm, la], dim=1)).reshape(B, Z, Y, X).amax(1, keepdim=True)
            outs.append(main + ls)
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

        self.layer_mix = nn.Conv2d(3 * LH, LH, 1)
        self.stem = nn.Conv2d(2 * LH, WIDTH, 1)

            nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(3 * HEAD, HEAD, 1), nn.ReLU(), nn.Conv2d(HEAD, 1, 1))
            for _ in self.footprints
        ])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

        hp = F.pad(h, (0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1))
        hb = hp[:, :Z]
        ha = hp[:, 2:]
        m = torch.cat([hb, h, ha], dim=2).reshape(B * Z, 3 * LH, Y, X)
        h = h + F.relu(self.layer_mix(m)).reshape(B, Z, LH, Y, X)
        s = torch.cat([h.amax(1), h.mean(1)], dim=1)
        f = F.relu(self.blocks(self.stem(s)))
        p = self.proj(f)
        outs = []
        for (dy, dx), head in zip(self.footprints, self.heads):
            pp = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            mx = F.max_pool2d(pp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            av = F.avg_pool2d(pp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            outs.append(head(torch.cat([p, mx, av], dim=1)))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

trials.hypothesis: Adds two learned softmax-attention pools over z, alongside r3c3's max and mean pools. Each cell can then read the exact features of one chosen layer, such as the build top or the next target layer, where max and mean blur across layers. This is the information that decides what a brick placed there would do. Cost is small (r≈1.0). Refuted if the 2-seed mean is at or below about 0.60.
trials.code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 32
BLOCKS = 2
HEAD = 16
LH = 24
NA = 2


class Block(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c):
        super().__init__()
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(c, c, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(c, c, 3, padding=1)

    def forward(self, x):
        return x + self.c2(F.relu(self.c1(F.relu(x))))


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.Z = int(spec.Z)
        self.footprints = [(int(fp[0]), int(fp[1])) for fp in spec.footprints]
        self.layer_in = nn.Conv2d(13, LH, 1)
        self.glob_in = nn.Conv2d(3, LH, 1)
        self.layer_mid = nn.Conv2d(LH, LH, 1)
        self.zatt = nn.Conv2d(LH, NA, 1)
        self.stem = nn.Conv2d((2 + NA) * LH, WIDTH, 1)
        self.register_buffer("zpos", torch.arange(self.Z).float() / max(self.Z - 1, 1))
        self.blocks = nn.Sequential(*[Block(WIDTH) for _ in range(BLOCKS)])
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, HEAD, 1)
        self.heads = nn.ModuleList([
            nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(3 * HEAD, HEAD, 1), nn.ReLU(), nn.Conv2d(HEAD, 1, 1))
            for _ in self.footprints
        ])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B, _, Y, X = obs.shape
        Z = self.Z
        v = obs[:, :4 * Z].reshape(B, 4, Z, Y, X)
        pz = F.pad(v, (0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1))
        below = pz[:, :, :Z]
        above = pz[:, :, 2:]
        zc = self.zpos.to(obs.dtype).view(1, 1, Z, 1, 1).expand(B, 1, Z, Y, X)
        x = torch.cat([v, below, above, zc], dim=1)
        x = x.permute(0, 2, 1, 3, 4).reshape(B * Z, 13, Y, X)
        gl = self.glob_in(obs[:, 4 * Z:4 * Z + 3]).unsqueeze(1)
        h = self.layer_in(x).reshape(B, Z, LH, Y, X) + gl
        h = F.relu(h).reshape(B * Z, LH, Y, X)
        h = F.relu(self.layer_mid(h))
        a = self.zatt(h).reshape(B, Z, NA, Y, X)
        w = torch.softmax(a, dim=1)
        h = h.reshape(B, Z, LH, Y, X)
        pools = [h.amax(1), h.mean(1)]
        for k in range(NA):
            pools.append((w[:, :, k:k + 1] * h).sum(1))
        s = torch.cat(pools, dim=1)
        f = F.relu(self.blocks(self.stem(s)))
        p = self.proj(f)
        outs = []
        for (dy, dx), head in zip(self.footprints, self.heads):
            pp = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            mx = F.max_pool2d(pp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            av = F.avg_pool2d(pp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            outs.append(head(torch.cat([p, mx, av], dim=1)))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

analyses.1: There are no trials yet. Starting-architecture seeds scored 0.068, 0.068, 0.258 and 0.068. Most runs seem to stop at a weak level, and a lucky seed sometimes breaks through. So any gain must clearly beat about 0.12, and it should hold across both seeds. The budget is only 32 updates of 4,096 steps each, and compute traded for size cuts samples one for one. Candidates should therefore stay near r≈1 and add useful structure, not size. The task is local. A brick is right at an anchor when its footprint matches target cells at the height where it will land, and that height depends on the build heights under the footprint. The starting 1x1 head sees only the anchor cell's features. Three single-change tests: (A) a head that pools features over each brick's footprint, (B) a deeper, narrower residual body at about the same compute, and (C) a more stable PPO initialisation to reduce seed collapse.
analyses.2: The 32-wide residual body (r1c2: 0.441 and 0.461) beat the start on both seeds by far more than seed noise. The start's seeds were 0.068 x3 and 0.258. r1c2 also costs less than the start (r=0.89), so it keeps the full sample budget. Depth and a wider receptive field (11x11) look like the main lever: the agent must judge landing height and the support or overhang order from nearby columns. The footprint-pooled head (r1c1, 0.18) may be a small gain, but its 2 seeds are within noise and it ran on the weak shallow body. Orthogonal init (r1c3, 0.069) did nothing. This round tests three things: (A) more depth at the same compute, with a receptive field covering the whole grid; (B) r1c2 plus the footprint-pooled head; (C) r1c2 with a whole-grid summary added inside each block.
analyses.3: The residual body accounts for most of the gain so far: r1c2 scored 0.45, about four times the starting architecture's 0.116. Adding the footprint-pooled head (r2c2) raised this to 0.505, but that is within seed noise of 0.45, so the evidence for the head is weak but positive. Going thinner and deeper (24 wide, 4 blocks) scored 0.40, so receptive field is not the bottleneck, and width may matter more than depth. Adding global context inside the blocks hurt (0.26) and was unstable across seeds. Orthogonal init did nothing. Every network with r up to 1 trains on the full sample budget, and all trials take under 75 s, so time is not a limit. What remains to test: a sharper head (an 'every footprint cell is fine' test is a min over the footprint), more width at the cost of fewer samples, and a stem that applies the same weights to every layer, so it can learn the relation between a column's top and the target at the next layer.
analyses.4: The clearest gain so far came from the per-layer encoder in r3c3, which uses shared weights across layers and pools over z. It reached 0.70 (seeds 0.57 and 0.83) against 0.505 for r2c2, which had the same body and head. The size of the jump suggests the gain is real and not seed noise. Two other results also look solid. Residual depth helped (r1c2 scored 0.45 against 0.12 for the start). The footprint-pooled head gave a smaller gain (r2c2 0.505 against r1c2 0.45). Three things clearly hurt. Raising compute above r=1 lost samples and collapsed (r3c2, 0.12). Global-context blocks scored lower (0.26). Min pooling did not help (0.41). Seed noise is large, about ±0.15 within a pair. For this last round, all three candidates keep r3c3 at r≤~1.05 and each makes one change to how the network reasons per layer: a per-layer footprint head, mixing between neighbouring layers, and attention pooling over z.
